extracted.intended_audience: eRA Commons users (PIs/PD-PIs, Signing Officials, grant administrators) performing grant closeout actions
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step procedural and policy guidance for completing closeout actions in eRA Commons (Final RPPR/FRP, Final Invention Statement, FRAM, FFR, TPPR) including role permissions, file upload/preview/submit behavior, and agency-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission authority (SO vs PD/PI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a signing official (SO) or a user with delegated report submit authority can submit the reports or other data; the program director/principal investigator (PD/PI) can upload, preview, delete and save the closeout report submission package, but cannot complete the final step to submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This note repeats across modules: only SOs (or users with delegated submit authority) see the Submit button and can finalize submissions. PD/PIs can prepare and save materials but not perform the final submission to the awarding agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR initiation and submission roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the PI can initiate the RPPR, and only the SO can submit it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After initiation a three-dot ellipsis menu appears for RPPR actions (e.g., Edit RPPR). Select Edit RPPR to fill out the RPPR; submission is restricted to SOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH/AHRQ Final Invention Statement policy & deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a Final Invention Statement (FIS) within 120 days following the termination of a grant award. The statement should include all inventions that were conceived or first reduced to practice during the course of work under the grant or award, from the original effective date of support through the date of completion or termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Agency-Specific Instruction applies to NIH and AHRQ-funded awards only; awards funded by other agencies may have different guidance—check the awarding agency's policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting inventions procedure (Final Invention Statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: To add an invention: type the Name of Inventor, Title of Invention, and the Date Reported to DHSS; click Add Invention and Save; confirm via popup and click Agree and Continue even if you have more inventions to add; inventions are listed under Added Inventions; as long as FIS is not submitted, a PI or SO can delete an item and save.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click Preview (Inventions Reported) to download a PDF copy of the filled form. When all inventions are listed click Submit to submit the invention statement to the awarding agency (only SO can submit). After submission the submitted PDF is available via View on the Closeout Status screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting no inventions procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To certify that no inventions exist: click Save with No Inventions; confirm that the Preview button is renamed to 'Preview (No Inventions Reported)'; click Submit (only SO sees Submit) which triggers a certification popup; click Agree and Continue to complete submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A success message appears and the submitted PDF (indicating no inventions) is available via View on the Closeout Status screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM purpose and when used
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Progress Report Additional Materials (FRAM) provides a means for recipients to enter, review, route, and submit information in response to specific request(s) by the program official (PO) for additional information related to the Final RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While reviewing a submitted Final RPPR the PO may request additional materials or a Revised Project Outcome; a FRAM task appears on the Closeout Status screen and the PD/PI is notified by email. Agency-specific differences apply (e.g., SAMHSA behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM screen sections and content guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The FRAM screen contains two distinct sections: the FRAM Upload Additional Materials section (for uploading one or more files) and the Revised Outcome section (to type or paste revised text for the RPPR section titled 'I. Outcomes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy guidance appears under the Revised Outcome section describing the type of description needed and includes links to samples of acceptable project outcomes. SAMHSA awards: the Revised Project Outcome section is not applicable for SAMHSA-funded awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM file upload and preview instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: To upload files: drag-and-drop in the 'Drop Files Here...' area or click browse to choose files; the drop area specifies how many files and what file types are allowed. For uploaded files you can click the Download icon to open/download the file or click the Delete icon to remove the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To discard an in-progress FRAM submission click the Delete button at bottom of screen (this does not delete prior submissions). To see what the FRAM submission includes: Save, then Preview (downloads a PDF summary containing uploaded files, uploader, any revised outcome saved, and file contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM submission, update, and notification behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Only SOs or users with delegated authority to submit reports can see and click the Submit button. After submitting a FRAM, a View action appears on Closeout Status to view a PDF of all documents and submission details. The FRAM Update action remains until acceptance of the Final RPPR, enabling additional uploads, but you cannot change files already submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An email notification is sent to the SO who submitted the FRAM, to the PI of the grant, and a separate notification to the PO. The PO may rescind approval of the Final RPPR or Final Progress Report at any time; if this occurs, the FRAM Update action appears again for submitting FRAM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised Project Outcome guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide a Revised Outcome: read the policy guidance in the Revised Outcome section prior to submitting; type or paste the revised outcome description into the text box provided; editing tools (bold, italic, bullets, numbering, indenting) are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH notices NOT-OD-17-022 and NOT-OD-17-037 for additional policy guidance. SAMHSA awardees should ignore the Revised Project Outcome section (not applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: TPPR requirement and purpose (SAMHSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: For awards granted by SAMHSA you are required to submit a Tangible Personal Property Report (TPPR) as part of the Closeout process. The purpose of the TPPR is to ensure any real or tangible personal property is accounted for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TPPR report should be prepared in accordance with instructions provided by the awarding agency; links to SAMHSA closeout guidance are referenced in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: TPPR initiation and submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: Either the PI or SO can initiate the TPPR. Drag-and-drop files into the 'Drop Files Here...' area or click browse to choose files (the area specifies allowed file types/count). Preview shows the entire submission as a PDF with application information, who uploaded the file and when, followed by the uploaded file contents. To save without submitting click Save; to finalize and submit click Submit (SO only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you change your mind before submission, click Delete to discard the TPPR. After saving but before submission an Edit button appears on Closeout Status allowing replacement of the uploaded file.

rubrics_metrics.name: TPPR post-initiation buttons and prior submissions behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: After a TPPR is saved but not submitted an Edit button appears to discard/upload a new file. After the TPPR is submitted but not accepted, the Initiate Tangible Personal Property button remains available and you can continue to upload and submit as many times as needed; each submission replaces the prior submission. After submission a View Prior Submission button becomes available to download the full submission PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The View Prior Submission PDF includes application information, uploader/time details, and the uploaded file contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Progress Report (FPR) applicability and distinction from RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Some agencies have a report called a Final Progress Report (FPR) for non-research awards. The Final Progress Report (FPR) should not be confused with the Final Research Performance Progress Report (FRPPR/RPPR), which is for research awards. The F. Changes form and the H. Budget form are not applicable for Final RPPRs; the I. Outcomes form is applicable only for Final RPPRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to submit an RPPR or see actions listed as RPPR or Process Final RPPR, refer to the RPPR Module instead of FPR guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: FPR initiation, editing, resubmission, and viewing prior submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Either the PD/PI or SO can initiate the Final Progress Report and upload file(s); both can save the document; only the SO can submit. To save without submitting click Save. After SO submits, users can initiate and submit new iterations and uploaded files after previous submissions are appended to previous submissions (prior submitted files cannot be removed). Use View Prior Submission to download the prior submission (DOC: ZIP with submission summary; SAMHSA: PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an FPR was initiated and saved (but not submitted) an Edit button appears allowing add/remove files and save; if the user is an SO the SO can submit. Agency-specific processes: DOC returns final progress report to recipient for changes; SAMHSA uses FRAM for additional requested materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Financial Report (FFR) requirement and system-specific submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Financial Report (FFR) is required for closeout and should be prepared according to instructions provided by the awarding agency. Commons users with the FSR role can see the Manage Final FFR action on the Closeout Status screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For DHHS-funded awards the FFR can be initiated from eRA Commons but users are redirected to the Payment Management System (PMS) to fill out and submit the report; users need appropriate PMS access. For DOC awards users initiate and fill out the FFR form within eRA Commons FFR module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-specific closeout requirements and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Closeout requirements and the types of actions/reports due vary by awarding agency (examples given: SAMHSA, DOC, VA). Typical actions include FFR, Final RPPR (research awards) or FPR (non-research awards), Final Invention Statement, FRAM, and TPPR (SAMHSA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide repeatedly notes to navigate to each topic via the Table of Contents and to consult agency-specific instructions within the eRA screens since wording and applicable sections differ by agency.
